newsitem.title: USA: KCBT HRW wheat ends lower, sets contract lows late.
newsitem.headline: KCBT HRW wheat ends lower, sets contract lows late.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed down, with contract lows set in July and September in late trade.
Most of the selling appeared to be speculative long liquidation motivated by the long holiday weekend and forecasts for active hard red winter wheat harvesting then in Kansas, traders said.
"It is too long a weekend to keep that position on," said one trader of the long liquidation.

The Kansas harvest has produced bountiful yields and has created talk the state output may exceed 400 million bushels. The previous 400-million Kansas harvest was in 1994 when output was 433.2 million. The record 1990 harvest was 472 million.

Futures finished down 7-1/4 to up four cents, with July off most at $3.25 per bushel which also was the contract low. September settled down 6-1/4 cents at $3.34-1/4, up slightly from the contract low of $3.34 set Thursday.
The market will be closed Friday in observance of Independence Day.
